newsitem.title: JAPAN: N.Korea sees resumption of talks on Japan ties.
newsitem.headline: N.Korea sees resumption of talks on Japan ties.

text.p: Japan and North Korea are expected to announce on Friday the resumption of on-again, off-again discussions aimed at normalising diplomatic ties, North Korean media said.

North Korea announced that from 2 p.m. (0500 GMT) it would broadcast a "special report concerning preparatory talks on the resumption of North Korea-Japan normalisation negotiations", said Radiopress news agency in a translation of a broadcast by the communist country's official radio network.
Separately, Japan's Foreign Ministry summoned the media for a news conference at the same hour by Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda. The ministry declined to disclose the topic.
Japan, which controlled Korea as a colony from 1910-45, normalised relations with South Korea in 1965 but has yet to establish diplomatic ties with North Korea.

Normalisation talks have been stalled since 1993 over Japan's persistent demands that North Korea clear up allegations that Japanese nationals were kidnapped by North Korean agents in the late 1970s and 1980s.

Tokyo has cited the unsolved kidnappings as the reason it refuses to join South Korea, the United States and international organisations in providing food aid to North Korea to stave off a severe famine experts say threatens the lives of millions of people.
